info.title: SignalDB API
info.description:
SignalDB admin, tenant-management, and query HTTP API

Every response whose request was traced carries the server's W3C trace context back to the caller: `Server-Timing: traceparent;desc="00-<trace-id>-<span-id>-<flags>"` (readable in browsers via the Performance API) and the equivalent `traceresponse` header, plus `Server-Timing` `dur` entries with server-side stage timings (always `total`, endpoint-specific stages where available) and `Timing-Allow-Origin: *` so cross-origin pages can read the timing entries. The headers are omitted when self-monitoring tracing is disabled.

get.summary: `GET /api/v1/query/sources` — the signal sources this tenant can query.
get.description:
List the signal sources available to the authenticated tenant and dataset, each with whether it is currently queryable. A registered signal whose table exists but holds no data is reported as available and empty, never omitted.

This is the one discovery call that is a GET rather than a `POST /api/v1/query` document: an IR document must name the source it queries (`from`), and "which sources exist" is the question that has no source to name. Every other discovery request — fields and values — is a document with a terminal `describe` stage and the `metadata` envelope, so this exception is bounded to this one route rather than a pattern to copy.

The answer comes from tenant metadata; it reads no signal data. The response is the same `metadata` envelope the `describe` documents return.

get.description:
Always 200, even when `[github]` is unconfigured (`configured: false`).
When configured, refreshes each installation's repository list from
GitHub; a refresh failure falls back to the last stored list, marked
`stale: true`, rather than failing the whole request.

post.description:
Attaches an installation that already exists on GitHub — e.g. one
already linked to another tenant on the same GitHub account — to
`tenant_id` directly, with no OAuth install flow. GitHub allows only one
App installation per account, so once one tenant has linked it, GitHub's
install-flow URL for a second tenant skips straight to its own
installation-management page instead of redirecting back here; this
endpoint is the escape hatch. Unlike [`start_github_link`]'s flow, there
is no user token to check the installation's `installation_id` against
— GitHub only scopes [`crate::github::GitHubApp::installation`] to *an*
installation of this App, not to any account the caller controls. A
`tenant:manage` grant is therefore not enough authorization on its own
(it would let a tenant admin attach, and so read the source of, any
other org that installed this deployment's App); this endpoint requires
`ctx.is_instance_admin`, the same principal that already holds the
App's private key. The same read-only-permission check the OAuth
callback performs is re-run here.

post.description:
Resolves a repo/ref/file/line reference to a bounded, cached source
snippet through the tenant's linked GitHub App installation(s). `400` on
a malformed request (empty `path`, `line: 0`, or an unsafe path —
containing a `..`, `.`, empty, or absolute segment — see
`crate::source_context::SourceRequest::new`); `403` when the path tenant
doesn't match the caller's authenticated tenant, or the caller has no
read access to any signal. Otherwise always `200`: an unconfigured
deployment, no covering installation, a missing file, or an out-of-range
line all answer `status: "unavailable"` with a `reason`, never an error —
the surrounding trace or profile view must render without the source
panel rather than fail.

get.description:
Unauthenticated probe the login page reads before rendering its
credential step. `oidc` is populated once `[auth.oidc]` is configured
*and* its provider discovery has succeeded — otherwise `null`, so an
unreachable issuer degrades to password-only rather than offering a
broken SSO button (change: oidc-login). `password_enabled` reflects
`[auth.oidc].disable_password_login`.

Reads state/nonce/PKCE-verifier from the pending-login cookie, exchanges
the code, validates the ID token, resolves the identity, and issues the
standard session on success — redirecting to the `redirect` target the
start request carried. Every validation failure — missing/invalid
pending cookie, state mismatch, a bad nonce/signature/expiry, an
unverified email on the link path, an allowlist refusal, or a disabled
user — collapses into the same generic `/login?error=sso_failed`
redirect with no session created and no disclosure of which check
failed; a resolved, enabled identity left with no tenant membership
after mapping sync instead redirects to `/login?error=no_membership`,
keeping the just-in-time-provisioned user row.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Authorization code returned by the IdP

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Opaque state value echoed back by the IdP

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: Present when the IdP failed the request before ever issuing a code

302.description: Redirect to the carried `redirect` target on success (session cookie set), `/login?error=sso_failed[&redirect=...]` on a generic validation failure, or `/login?error=no_membership&redirect=...` when the user ends up with no tenant membership

get.description:
302s to the IdP's authorization endpoint with a fresh PKCE challenge,
`state`, and `nonce`, and sets the signed pending-login cookie carrying
what the callback needs to complete the exchange, including the
validated `redirect` return target. 404 when OIDC isn't configured; 503
naming the issuer while discovery hasn't (yet) succeeded.

parameters.name: redirect
parameters.description: Same-origin path to return to after a successful login; anything else (or absent) falls back to `/logs`

302.description: Redirect to the IdP's authorization endpoint; sets the signed pending-login cookie

ApiErrorBody.description:
The JSON envelope every query-surface error responds with: `status` is
always `"error"`, `errorType` a stable low-cardinality code, `error` a
human-readable message, and `retryAfterMs` present only on rate-limit
rejections. Exists as a real (rather than `serde_json::json!`-built)
type so the OpenAPI document can declare its schema on the `429`
response of every rate-limited operation.

retryAfterMs.description:
Milliseconds until the request would be admitted; present only when
`errorType` is `"rate_limited"`.

installation_id.description:
A GitHub App installation id that already exists for this App —
e.g. one already linked to another tenant on the same GitHub
account, or read off GitHub's own installation settings page.

The canonical type the type authority committed for this key, per
dataset/signal/level it has been observed in, and how many values
arrived with a different type (kept, but not typed-queryable). Absent

resolutions.description: Present when `keys=` was given: one resolution per requested key.

AttributeTypeRecord.description:
One stored row for an attribute key, scoped to a single dataset, signal,
and attribute level within a tenant.

schemas.description: All table schema types SignalDB knows how to provision.

at_least.description:
When true the collector hit its cap: the true count is at least
`estimate`, not equal to it.

Whether every required `[public]` field (OTLP gRPC/HTTP, API URL) has
been explicitly set. `false` means at least one of those URLs below is

ConsentContextResponse.description:
Context the consent screen renders: the requesting client and the tenants
the signed-in user may grant.

client_name.description: Display name of the requesting client, if it registered one.

tenants.description: Tenants the user may grant access to.

ConsentDataset.description:
A dataset within a tenant the consenting user may restrict a grant to
(D5).

ConsentDecision.description:
Consent decision posted by the explore-UI (change: mcp-oauth-dcr;
generalized to a set of tenants by mcp-multi-tenant-oauth-grants D2/D6).
The user is authenticated by their session cookie; `tenant_grants` is
their chosen set of one or more tenants to grant, each with its own
independent dataset restriction.

The legacy singular `tenant`/`dataset_id` fields are not accepted (the
latter removed in the multi-dataset-key-restriction change, D8): a
request body carrying either is rejected rather than silently ignored,
since dropping it would grant unrestricted or differently-scoped access
than the caller asked for.

approved.description: Whether the user approved (`true`) or denied (`false`).

code_challenge.description: The PKCE `code_challenge` from the authorization request.

redirect_uri.description: The redirect URI to return to (must be registered for the client).

resource.description: Requested resource (audience); must match the configured MCP resource.

scope.description: Requested scope (space-delimited); read scopes only are granted.

state.description: Opaque `state` to echo back to the client.

tenant_grants.description:
The set of tenants the user grants access to (each must be one they
belong to). Must be non-empty and name each tenant at most once.

ConsentDecisionResponse.description:
Result of a consent decision: the URL the browser should navigate to (the
client's redirect URI carrying either the authorization `code` or an
`error`).

redirect.description: The absolute redirect URL to navigate to.

ConsentTenant.description: A tenant the consenting user may grant a connector access to.

datasets.description:
Datasets in the tenant, so the consent screen can offer a per-tenant
"only these datasets" checklist (D5).

role.description: The user's role in the tenant.

ConsentTenantGrant.description:
One tenant (and optional dataset restriction) the user grants in a
consent decision (design: mcp-multi-tenant-oauth-grants D2/D6). Mirrors
[`common::catalog::TenantGrant`]'s shape; kept as a router-local request
DTO (rather than reusing that type directly) so it can derive
[`ToSchema`] for the OpenAPI spec.

dataset_ids.description:
Dataset set to restrict this tenant's grant to (D5/D6). Omitted or
`null` grants unrestricted access to the tenant. A non-empty array
restricts the grant to exactly that set; every named dataset must
belong to `tenant_id`. An explicit empty array is rejected (D1a), as
is any non-empty selection while
`[auth].dataset_restriction_rollout_complete` is `false` (stricter
than the API-key rule — OAuth has no legacy column to fall back to).

tenant_id.description: The tenant being granted (must be one the user belongs to).

CostMode.description: Which tier answered a discovery request, and therefore what it cost.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the tables were created for.

CreateUserRequest.description: Request body for creating a human user with an initial tenant membership.

password.description: Password (hashed server-side; must be at least 12 characters).

tenant.description: Tenant to grant the initial membership in.

CurrentSessionResponse.description:
`GET /ui/session`'s response: the signed-in user, the memberships the
session may enter, and the auto-selected tenant/dataset.

dataset.description:
Always serialized, `null` when no tenant is auto-selected — not an
omittable field.

tenant.description:
Always serialized, `null` when no tenant is auto-selected — not an
omittable field.

DatasetTables.description:
The tables provisioned in a single dataset, as part of
[`ListTablesResponse::datasets`].

DemoLoginConfig.description:
The demo account's credentials, returned by `login_config` only when
`[demo].enabled` is true (change: demo-mode) so the login page can offer
an "Explore the demo" shortcut.

brief.description: The registry's one-line description, when a registry defines it.

oneOf.description: An approximate distinct-value count, when statistics exist.

coverage.description:
The fraction of the tenant's records carrying it, when statistics
exist. Absent means unknown — never defaulted to a number that could be
mistaken for a measurement.

deprecated.description: Whether a registry marks it deprecated.

filterable.description:
Whether a predicate may address it (retrieval-only fields are listed,
not hidden).

oneOf.description:
The OTel attribute level, when known. Statistics carry no level, so an
observed key reports `null` rather than a guess.

name.description: The logical, dotted OTel-native name — directly usable in a predicate.

origin.description: The tier this item came from.

type.description: The canonical value type a literal is coerced to.

DiscoveredSource.description: One signal source available to the tenant.

available.description:
Whether the tenant can query it. A registered signal with no data is
available and empty, never omitted.

name.description: The name an IR document's `from` names.

count.description: How often it was observed, when the tier that produced it counts.

DiscoveryCost.description: What a discovery answer cost and how far it can be trusted.

approximate.description:
Whether the answer is approximate — a bounded sketch of the most
frequent values rather than the exact set. A declared value set is
exact; a statistics- or scan-derived one is not, and saying so is the
difference between a suggestion and a claim.

as_of.description:
How recent the statistics behind the answer are (as the catalog stores
it). `null` means no statistics exist yet.

sampled.description: Whether the answer is sampled, and therefore possibly incomplete.

window_scoped.description:
Whether the answer is scoped to the requested time window. Maintained
statistics carry no time dimension, so a metadata answer says `false`
rather than implying the range narrowed it.

EntityAttribute.description: An attribute referenced by an entity, with its role.

extends.description: Entity this one extends (bare name), if any.

extended_by.description: `namespace/entity` names of entities extending this one.

metrics.description: Metric names associated with this entity (from every visible registry).

EntityHit.description: A resolved entity definition tagged with provenance.

EnumMember.description: One member of an enum attribute type.

FieldOrigin.description: Which metadata tier a discovered item came from.

Filterability.description: Whether predicates may address a field.

levels.description:
One flat array per depth level. `format: "single"` uses
`[offset_delta, total, self, name_index]` quadruples; `"double"`
uses `[off_l, total_l, self_l, off_r, total_r, self_r, name_index]`.

maxSelf.description: Largest self value of any block, for color scaling.

names.description: Function name table referenced by block name indices.

FlamebearerMetadata.description: Metadata describing how to interpret flamebearer values.

format.description: `"single"` for one profile set, `"double"` for a diff.

name.description: Display name of the rendered profile/query.

sampleRate.description: Sample rate in Hz; 100 is the Pyroscope default for CPU profiles.

spyName.description: Profiler that produced the data, when known (e.g. "gospy").

FlamegraphResult.description:
A flamegraph in Pyroscope flamebearer encoding — the same shape and
aggregation `/pyroscope/render` returns, reused here so the native Query
IR surface can retrieve an actual profile payload (bounded, aggregated)
rather than raw `samples_json`/`stacktraces_json`. See `query-ir-core`'s
"Profile flamegraph retrieval" requirement.

levels.description:
One entry per depth level; each level is a flat sequence of
`[offset_delta, total, self, name_index]` quadruples.

locations.description:
Source location for each entry in `names`, aligned by index; `None`
(or the array is shorter than `names`) where unknown. See
`common::profile::Flamegraph::locations`.

max_self.description: Largest self value of any block, used for color scaling.

names.description: Function name table referenced by the blocks' name indices.

total.description: Total value of the root (sum of all samples).

truncated.description:
`true` when more than `FLAMEGRAPH_PROFILE_CAP` (1,000) profile rows
matched — a row-count cap, not a byte-size one — and the flamegraph
was aggregated over only the first 1,000 of them.

FrameLocation.description: A function's source location, carried alongside a flamegraph name entry.

file.description: Source file path, as reported by the profiler.

GitHubInstallationResponse.description: One linked installation, as reported by [`list_github_installations`].

manage_url.description: GitHub's own installation-settings page for this installation.

repositories.description:
The installation's covered repositories, as `"owner/name"` full
names.

repositories_synced_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the last successful repository-list refresh.

stale.description:
`true` when the live GitHub refresh failed and `repositories` is the
last successfully fetched copy rather than a fresh one.

app_slug.description: The App's URL slug, present only when `configured`.

configured.description:
`false` when `[github]` is absent (or failed to build) — the
endpoint answers 200 rather than 404 so a caller can render "GitHub
is not set up" without special-casing an error status.

expires_at.description:
RFC 3339 timestamp naming when the state token (and so this link
attempt) expires.

install_url.description:
GitHub's install page to redirect the admin's browser to. Carries
the single-use state token as its `state` query parameter.

GrantedTenant.description:
One tenant a credential's grant reaches, with its own dataset-set
restriction — the `whoami`/`/oauth/introspect` output shape (change:
mcp-multi-tenant-oauth-grants D4/D5). Mirrors
[`common::catalog::TenantGrant`]; kept as a router-local response DTO so
it can derive [`utoipa::ToSchema`].

GraphEdge.description: Calls from `source` to `target` in the window.

error_rate.description: Share (0..1) of the calls with error status.

rate.description: Calls per second: `count` over the window length in seconds.

GraphNode.description: A service or an uninstrumented dependency.

error_rate.description: Share (0..1) of the node's server/consumer spans with error status.

id.description:
Stable identity, distinct from `name`: `service:<name>` for a
service, `external:<kind>:<name>` for an external dependency, and
`external:<kind>:unnamed:<caller>` for an external with no naming
attribute. Edges reference nodes by this id.

name.description:
Display name: the service name, or for an external node the first present of
`db.namespace`, `messaging.destination.name`, `rpc.service`,
`server.address`, `peer.service` (`unnamed <kind>` if none is set).

p95_ns.description: p95 duration of the node's server/consumer spans, in nanoseconds.

request_rate.description: Service nodes with server/consumer spans only: requests per second.

GraphNodeKind.description:
Whether a node reported spans of its own or was inferred from a client
or producer span with no instrumented callee.

HeatmapAxisX.description: Epoch-aligned time axis with a fixed nanosecond step.

HeatmapResult.description:
Complete axes plus one non-zero heatmap cell. Missing declared coordinates
represent zero, making the Flight payload sparse without hiding the window.

LabelsResponse.description: Response body of the label-names / label-values endpoints.

datasets.description:
The same tables, grouped by dataset.

Defaulted on deserialization so an older client-recorded response
(or a hand-written test fixture) that predates this field still
parses.

tables.description: List of tables for the tenant, flat across all of its datasets.

LogicalField.description:
One logical (client-visible, OTel-native) field, as registered in
[`common::schema::logical::LogicalSchema`].

level.description:
`resource` | `scope` | `record`, absent when the field isn't
attribute-scoped (a plain `String` here, not `Option<AttributeLevel>`
— utoipa emits a nullable `$ref` enum as `oneOf: [{type: null}, ref]`,
which the progenitor-generated Rust SDK client can't parse).

LogicalFieldKind.description: The semantic role of a logical field.

LogicalType.description: The client-visible type of a logical field.

LoginConfigResponse.description:
`GET /ui/session/config`'s response: which credentials the login page
may offer. `oidc` is `null` until an OIDC provider is configured.

oneOf.description:
Always serialized, `null` unless `[demo].enabled` is true (change:
demo-mode) — not an omittable field.

Always serialized, `null` until an OIDC provider is configured — not
an omittable field.

ManageCreateApiKeyRequest.description:
`dataset_ids` mirrors [`signaldb_api::CreateApiKeyRequest`] (D1a): omitted
or `null` creates an unrestricted key, a non-empty array restricts it,
and an explicit empty array or duplicate name is rejected. The legacy
singular `dataset_id` field is not accepted — `deny_unknown_fields`
rejects a request body still sending it, rather than silently dropping
it and creating an unrestricted key when the caller asked for a
restricted one.

ManageCreatedApiKey.description:
201 response body for API key creation via the management API.

Fields mirror the previous `json!` body exactly (including `null` for
absent `name`), preserving the wire format.

ManageError.description: Error response body for the tenant-scoped resource endpoints.

ManageUpdateApiKeyRequest.description:
Body for `PATCH /api/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/api-keys/{key_id}`.
Absent fields are left untouched. `dataset_ids`/`clear_dataset_restriction`
mirror [`signaldb_api::UpdateApiKeyRequest`] (D1a); the legacy singular
`dataset_id` field is rejected via `deny_unknown_fields` rather than
silently dropped.

allowed_origins.description:
Replacement allowed-origins set (non-empty; an explicit empty array
is rejected). Omitted/`null` leaves the current restriction
unchanged. Mutually exclusive with `clear_allowed_origins: true`.

clear_allowed_origins.description:
Clear an existing allowed-origins restriction back to unrestricted.
Must not be combined with a non-empty `allowed_origins` in the same
request.

clear_dataset_restriction.description:
Clear an existing dataset restriction back to unrestricted. Must not
be combined with a non-empty `dataset_ids` in the same request.

dataset_ids.description:
Replacement dataset set (non-empty; an explicit empty array is
rejected). Omitted/`null` leaves the current restriction unchanged.
Mutually exclusive with `clear_dataset_restriction: true`.

scopes.description: Replacement scope list (non-empty, drawn from the shared vocabulary).

granted_by.description:
`"local"` (granted via this API/CLI/MCP) or `"oidc_mapping"` (synced
from an OIDC group claim, change: oidc-login). A local and a mapped
row can coexist for the same user, yielding two response rows that
differ only by this field — the UI keys on `user_id` + `granted_by`.

MembershipRole.description:
Role a user holds within a tenant.

Stored as lowercase TEXT in the `tenant_memberships` table, matching
the `CHECK(role IN ('admin', 'member', 'viewer'))` constraint.

MetadataKind.description: What a discovery answer is about.

MetadataResult.description: The payload of a `metadata` result envelope.

cost.description: Which tier answered, and how far the answer can be trusted.

hint.description:
The Query IR request that produced this answer by reading data, or —
when nothing covers the request — the one that would compute it.

truncated.description: Whether a documented limit cut the list short.

MetricAttribute.description: An attribute declared on a metric.

entity_associations.description: Entity type names this metric describes.

MetricHit.description: A resolved metric definition tagged with provenance.

resolutions.description: Present when `keys=` was given: one resolution per requested name.

MultiQueryIrRequest.description:
A multi-query document (D5): several named IR queries — each required to
declare `result: "series"` — plus formulas evaluated over their results
after every inner query has run. Series join on an identical label set
and timestamp; a formula input missing a series present in another
contributes nothing to the join, and a zero divisor drops the point,
rather than either erroring.

result.description: Always `"series"` — a formula document has no other shape.

OidcLoginConfig.description: A single-sign-on provider offered by the login-configuration probe.

name.description: Display name shown on the "Continue with {name}" control.

authority.description:
`host[:port]`, with the port included only when the configured URL
states one explicitly.

PhysicalField.description: One physical (storage) column, as resolved from `schemas.toml`.

PhysicalSchema.description: One resolved table-schema version for one signal source.

ProcessorError.description: Error body for the processors API.

created_at.description:
RFC3339 timestamp, as stored (`StoredRegistry` follows the same
string-typed convention for the same reason: one dialect-agnostic
decode path in the store, see `row_to_record`).

dataset.description:
The dataset *name* this processor applies to, or `None` for a
tenant-wide rule.

status.description:
`"invalid"` when the stored statements currently fail to compile
(skipped at apply time, never blocking ingest); `"ok"` otherwise.

ProcessorResponse.description: A processor row plus its compiled status.

ProcessorSpec.description:
Caller-supplied processor definition, without tenant scoping or
timestamps — the body of a create/replace request.

ProcessorWriteResponse.description:
Every write response carries the cross-process propagation bound for the
change: the `ProcessorRegistry` cache TTL, in seconds.

ProfileSummary.description:
Summary of a stored profile linked to a trace, without the bulky
stack/sample payloads.

QualifiedEntityRole.description: An entity role qualified by the registry that declares it.

QueryFormula.description:
One named formula in a [`MultiQueryIrRequest`] (D5): arithmetic
(`+ - * /`, numeric constants, parentheses) over the request's own query
names, e.g. `"errors / total"`.

name.description:
The formula's identity: tags each output series' `labels` under the
`formula` key, so a request with several formulas stays distinguishable.

QueryIrRequest.description:
A versioned Query IR request document.

The `pipeline` stages are opaque JSON objects at the HTTP boundary — the
querier validates and lowers them per the versioned IR contract. See the
`query-ir-core` capability for the full stage/predicate grammar.

focus.description: `graph` only: restrict to this service's neighbourhood.

from.description: The registered signal source: `logs`, `traces`, or profile-summary `profiles`.

irVersion.description: IR document version (the server accepts a bounded range).

pipeline.description: Ordered transform stages (opaque objects; see the IR spec).

result.description:
Declared result envelope: `rows`, `series`, `table`, `heatmap`,
(for the `profiles` source only) `flamegraph`, or (for the `traces`
source, irVersion 8+) `graph`.

trace_id.description: `graph` only: restrict to the services and calls of one trace.

QueryIrRequestBody.description:
The `POST /api/v1/query` request body: either a single IR document or a
[`MultiQueryIrRequest`], discriminated by the presence of `queries` — a
document without it is a single [`QueryIrRequest`], so an ordinary
request needs no wrapper key.

QueryIrResponse.description:
The single canonical response contract. `result` discriminates which fields
are populated: `rows`/`table` fill `columns` + `rows`; `series` fills
`series` + `step_ns`; `heatmap` fills `heatmap`; `flamegraph` fills
`flamegraph`; `graph` fills `graph`.

oneOf.description:
Present iff `result == "flamegraph"` — `Some` even when zero profiles
matched, so an empty match set stays distinguishable from "this
response has no flamegraph at all" (i.e. a different envelope).
Present iff `result == "graph"` — the service dependency graph.

Present iff `result == "metadata"` — what a `describe` document asked
about, with the provenance and cost of the answer.

warnings.description:
Non-fatal diagnostics about this query. Empty (and omitted) when the
server has nothing to report; a warning never suppresses the result.

window.description: The resolved absolute window the query ran over.

QueryRange.description:
The query time range. `from`/`to` are timestamp literal **strings**: RFC3339,
a relative anchor (`now-1h`), or a nanosecond integer as a numeric string
(`"1700000000000000000"`). Kept a `String` so the emitted schema and the
generated clients match exactly what the endpoint accepts.

QueryWarning.description:
A non-fatal diagnostic about a query that still produced a result. A
warning never changes the result: it explains something the caller
probably did not intend, so a client can surface it next to the data.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable identifier — clients branch on this, not on
`message`. Today `unknown_group_by_field` and
`no_attribute_statistics`.

field.description: The document field the warning is about, when it names one.

message.description: Human-readable explanation, safe to show verbatim.

suggestions.description: Field names close to `field` that the source does declare, best first.

document.description:
The registry document in the OpenTelemetry Weaver semantic-convention
model (`name`, `version`, `schema_url`, `dependencies`, `groups`).

RegistryResponse.description: A registry with its document (the uploaded Weaver-model file, verbatim).

RenderResponse.description: Response body of `GET /pyroscope/render` (and the diff variant).

leftTicks.description: Total baseline ticks; present when `format` is `"double"`.

rightTicks.description: Total comparison ticks; present when `format` is `"double"`.

ResolvedWindow.description: The resolved absolute time window, echoed for reproducibility/replay.

ResultSeries.description: One time series in a `series` result.

Role.description: Role of an attribute within an entity.

SchemaError.description: Error body for the schema API.

errors.description: Validation errors with document paths (422 only).

ServiceGraph.description:
The assembled graph. `dropped_nodes` counts the nodes removed by the
server-side node cap (`[querier].graph_max_nodes`).

SessionMembership.description:
A tenant the signed-in user may select, returned by `POST /ui/session`
and `GET /ui/session` so the UI can present a picker instead of
free-text tenant entry.

SessionUser.description: The signed-in user, as reported by `GET /ui/session`.

is_demo.description:
True when this is the `[demo]` read-only account (change:
demo-mode), so the UI can show a "read-only" badge and hide
mutating navigation without hardcoding the demo username.

SourceContextAvailability.description:
Whether source context can be served for a tenant at all — the UI's
read-level probe for showing or hiding "View source" (the installation
*list* is a management-only endpoint that ordinary readers cannot call).

linked.description: The tenant has linked at least one GitHub App installation.

context_lines.description:
Lines of context on each side of `line`; defaults to
[`DEFAULT_CONTEXT_LINES`] and is clamped to
[`crate::source_context::MAX_CONTEXT_LINES`].

line.description: The 1-based line number to center the snippet on.

path.description: The file path within the repository.

ref.description:
The ref (branch, tag, or commit SHA) to read the file at. Omit it to
read the repository's default branch.

repository.description:
`owner/name`, or a GitHub URL naming the repository (`https://github.com/owner/name`,
`owner/name.git`, ...). Omit it to probe every repository covered by
the tenant's linked GitHub installations by path alone.

SourceContextResponse.description:
Response body for [`source_context`]. Always `200` for a well-formed
request, whether or not a snippet could be served.

oneOf.description:
Why no snippet was served; present only when `status` is
`"unavailable"`.
The resolved snippet; present only when `status` is `"available"`.

SourceSnippet.description:
A bounded window of source lines around one line of one file, plus
enough metadata to render and link to it.

html_url.description: GitHub's `html_url` for the file, with a `#L{line}` fragment.

line.description: The 1-based line number the snippet is centered on.

lines.description: The window of source lines, `start_line..=start_line + lines.len() - 1`.

path.description: The file path within the repository.

ref.description:
The ref the caller asked for; `None` means the repository's default
branch.

repository.description: The `"owner/name"` repository that served the snippet.

sha.description: The blob's `sha`, as GitHub reports it.

events.description:
Span events (annotations, exceptions). Omitted when empty. Exceptions are
the event named `exception`, carrying `exception.message`/`.type`/
`.stacktrace` in their attributes.

name.description: Span name intrinsic (Tempo exposes it as `name` on spanset spans).

parentSpanID.description:
Parent span id; empty/absent for root spans. Needed by clients that
reconstruct the span hierarchy (e.g. waterfall views).

SpanEvent.description: A span event in the Tempo API span shape.

StatementError.description: One compile error, positioned to a statement and (where known) a column.

dataset.description:
The dataset this table belongs to.

Defaulted on deserialization so an older client-recorded response
(or a hand-written test fixture) that predates this field still
parses.

TagScope.description:
GET /api/search/tags?scope=<resource|span|intrinsic>

`rename_all = "lowercase"` matters here: the Tempo API (and Grafana's
Tempo datasource, which is what actually sends this) uses lowercase
scope values. Without it, serde only accepts the Rust variant names
(`Resource`/`Span`/`Intrinsic`) and every real client 400s (#1073).

TenantResponse.description:
Superset tenant response: the catalog-backed identity fields
(`id`/`name`/`default_dataset`/`source`/timestamps) every caller of the
old admin surface relied on, unchanged.

processors.description:
Processors to apply, in the given order; when omitted, the tenant's
stored processors for `signal`/`dataset` are used instead.

processor.description:
Name of the processor this statement belongs to, so results from
multiple processors (each restarting `index` at 0) can be told apart.

Timeline.description: Optional per-interval sample counts for the render timeline.

startTime.description: Start of the timeline, unix seconds.

profiles.description:
Summaries of profiles linked to this trace; present only when the
client asked for them via `include_profiles`.

UnavailableReason.description: Why a lookup could not serve a snippet.

UpdateTenantRequest.description: Request body for updating an existing tenant.

UserResponse.description: Response returned when a user is created (never includes the password hash).

instance_admin.description: Whether the user is an instance administrator.

ValidationError.description: A validation failure at a location in the document.

ValidationReport.description: Outcome of validating a document without storing it.

ValueOrigin.description: Where a suggested value came from.

WhoamiIdentityResponse.description: The non-null identity contract shared by generated clients.

dataset_ids.description:
The credential's own dataset-set restriction, if any; `null`/absent
means unrestricted. See [`WhoamiResponse::dataset_ids`].

user_id.description: Stable authenticated user ID. Empty for API key credentials.

tempo_api.v2.TagValuesResponse.description:
GET /api/v2/search/tag/.service.name/values

Todo: Add types to values

See <https://grafana.com/docs/tempo/latest/api_docs/#search-tag-values-v2>

RateLimited.description: Rate limited: the tenant's request budget for this dimension is exhausted. `Retry-After` states whole seconds (rounded up, at least 1) until the request would be admitted, computed from the token bucket's actual state.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds (rounded up, at least 1) until the request would be admitted

X-RateLimit-Burst.description: The tenant's burst allowance for the rejected dimension

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The tenant's per-second budget for the rejected dimension

schema.description:
The JSON envelope every query-surface error responds with: `status` is
always `"error"`, `errorType` a stable low-cardinality code, `error` a
human-readable message, and `retryAfterMs` present only on rate-limit
rejections. Exists as a real (rather than `serde_json::json!`-built)
type so the OpenAPI document can declare its schema on the `429`
response of every rate-limited operation.

retryAfterMs.description:
Milliseconds until the request would be admitted; present only when
`errorType` is `"rate_limited"`.
